- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward to reflect bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent high, adjust downward to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after recent spikes; cap upward revisions if sentiment is weak or trending down.  
- If forecast shows strong mean reversion (e.g., dropping sharply after a peak), verify with sentiment — if sentiment is neutral or negative, don’t force reversal.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% and sentiment is positive, assume momentum is sustained; if sentiment turns negative, reduce forecast slope.  
- If forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a “lag correction” — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next period if sentiment remains stable.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.2 in 3 consecutive days), avoid sharp directional forecasts — use smoother, trend-following adjustments.
